To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) plant-based foods have far lower environmental impacts, per unit of nutritional value, than animal-based foods; and (ii) the environmental benefits of reducing meat consumption and switching to more efficient agricultural production are much greater than the benefits of switching to organic or grass-fed production.
Plant-based foods have the least impact on the environment and human health, followed by animal-sourced foods that require less agricultural land, feed, and inputs.

(1) organic and conventional agriculture have similar impacts, (2) grass-fed beef has larger environmental impacts than grain-fed beef, (3) non-trawling and aquaculture have smaller impacts than trawling, (4) agricultural input efficiency improvements offer environmental benefits, and (5) food choice has the largest impacts on the environment.

understanding how alternative agricultural systems and food choices impact the environment.
understanding the environmental impacts of agricultural systems, agricultural input use efficiency, and food choices.
